INSTRUCTIONS: Tag referenced workspace files with @
INPUT:
team we need to address the redis cluster cache stampede that occurred during this morning's flash sale. first please check redis dot conf in the config directory to confirm that maxmemory-policy is configured to volatile-lru and verify that our client connection pool limits are set to twenty thousand connections. next inspect sentinel dot py in the cluster package and check file reference at services slash cache manager dot ts in the services directory. the primary incident trigger was a sudden cache invalidation cascade when five thousand concurrent checkout workers attempted to recalculate inventory balances simultaneously after key expiration. to prevent recurrent stampedes we must implement probabilistic early expiration using xfetch algorithm with a beta value of one point two and set background refresh timeouts to ten seconds scratch that five seconds. in addition update sentinel dot py to ensure that automatic sentinel failover triggers after three consecutive unresponsive ping probes spaced two seconds apart rather than the current thirty second timeout. do not disable master-replica replication sync under any circumstances during failover testing. the database team lead requires that we verify fallback read throughput against read replicas and establish automated grafana alerts when redis memory fragmentation ratio exceeds one point five. also confirm that all worker threads log redis connection timeouts to datadog with structured error tags including client ip address tenant id and operation latency before concluding the remediation cycle. furthermore our edge caching layer must enforce a minimum time to live of one hundred twenty seconds on inventory metadata to avoid upstream redis queries during momentary network partitions between edge gateways and core database pods. the reliability engineering team will run automated load tests simulating fifteen thousand transactions per second against the staging cluster to ensure latency remains under twenty-five milliseconds across ninety-nine percent of requests. regarding sentinel cluster quorum we must verify that all three sentinel pods run on independent availability zones and configure down-after-milliseconds to five thousand milliseconds across each node. the client connection pools in auth service and order worker must initialize backoff retries using full jitter with a base interval of one hundred milliseconds capped at two thousand milliseconds. incident coordinators should also review runbook documentation in docs slash runbooks slash redis underscore failover dot md to ensure that emergency manual failover procedures accurately reflect the latest cluster endpoint topology. we must also confirm that redis persistent append-only files are synced every second on replica disks and verify that background rewrite tasks do not trigger memory allocation spikes during active peak traffic windows. finally schedule an operational readiness review for thursday afternoon with the infrastructure engineering manager to audit all configuration diffs and approve deployment to production.
